A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QZO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original NLP fine-tuning results, memory and computation measurements, a clipping ablation, and Stable Diffusion image-generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports SGD fine-tuning comparisons, clipping-threshold sensitivity, and experiments using different training-set partitions.

M1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same scale perturbations, frozen quantized weights, directional derivative clipping, seed regeneration, and nonnegative scale updates. No proposed algorithm component or update procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SST-2, RTE, CB, BoolQ, SQuAD, and the same four styles from the Styled Image Dataset. The diffusion experiments move to Appendix B. The new threshold and partition analyses remain within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 replace LoRA with full-parameter, 16-bit SGD fine-tuning. Figure 1 similarly replaces LoRA with SGD fine-tuning while retaining the previous full-fine-tuning memory reference, now explicitly labeled AdamW. Table 3 removes the Llama-2-13B LoRA comparator without replacement. Zero-shot and MeZO comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new SGD comparator uses an initial learning rate of 8e-4, linear decay, and batch size 8. Added analyses vary the clipping threshold and training-set partition. Existing QZO hyperparameters, benchmark sample counts, evaluation metrics, and memory-profiling procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's DDC on/off training traces, v2 adds clipping-threshold sensitivity on Llama-2-7B/SST-2 and training-set sampling robustness across all five OPT-6.7B tasks. Figure 3 and Table 4 substantially expand the analysis of stability, hyperparameter sensitivity, and dependence on sampled training data.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty summaries. v2 Table 4 introduces partition seeds 0, 1, and 2, individual outcomes, averages, and reported 95% confidence intervals across five OPT-6.7B tasks. This is newly reported statistical evidence; Tables 1–3 remain point estimates, and no increase in their run counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing QZO, MeZO, and zero-shot benchmark scores are retained, with some memory values merely rounded. LoRA results are removed and new SGD results replace them in Tables 1–2. For Llama-2-7B SQuAD, QZO remains at 85.5 F1, while the reference changes from LoRA at 89.9 to SGD fine-tuning at 83.7; this changes the comparator and ranking, not QZO's performance. Figure 3 and Table 4 add threshold- and partition-specific results.

T1.justification: v2 repairs the missing squared factors and norm notation in main-text Eq. 7 and states the variance derivation explicitly coordinatewise in Eq. 8. Theorem 1, its unbiasedness proof, and the underlying variance argument already appear in v1 Appendix A; their relocation does not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The central claims remain scale-based quantized fine-tuning with DDC, compatibility with scalar and codebook quantization, over 18-fold memory savings, and performance comparable to MeZO. Stable Diffusion disappears from the abstract and introduction but its feasibility claim remains in the conclusion and Appendix B.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking small clipping thresholds to underfitting, large thresholds to instability, and partition results to sampling robustness. It recommends more accurate quantization and removes the conclusion's standalone full-precision performance-gap limitation, while narrowing the main-results gap discussion to some tasks. The diffusion mechanism explanations are retained in Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 documents SGD settings and an A100 80GB GPU, replacing the LoRA implementation and two-GPU disclosure. Appendix B specifies NF4 where v1 stated only 4-bit BitsAndBytes quantization; this adds specificity without establishing an experimental change. A prospective public code-release statement is added while the same project link remains.

R1.justification: The LoRA discussion and Hu et al. reference are removed, along with several other bibliography entries, including work on extremely sparse zeroth-order fine-tuning and sub-4-bit compressed-model fine-tuning. The broader positioning relative to MeZO, GaLore, and post-training quantization remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized into setup, main results, and ablation sections. Diffusion experiments move into Appendix B, while the theorem and variance derivation move into the methodology. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are refocused, and numbered citations become author–year citations. This substantially reorganizes the document despite considerable retained prose.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document-wide title, heading, and running-header layout; enlarges Figure 1 from a wrapped display to full width; revises its comparator legend; and adds Figure 3 and Table 4. Tables are reordered or shortened, and diffusion figures are resized and relocated. The diffusion images and DDC trace graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new threshold analysis and partition confidence intervals provide useful stability evidence absent from v1, and the SGD experiments add a full-parameter reference. However, these comparisons replace LoRA rather than supplementing it, and the supervised Llama-2-13B reference disappears entirely. Thus, stronger robustness evidence accompanies reduced comparison coverage for the paper's memory-efficiency claims. With the core QZO results unchanged, these material competing effects do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or decline.
